key_insight: CAPE embeds cavitation physics directly into acoustic perturbation equations so cavitation-generated sound sources can be resolved inside the flow field.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a practical way to predict, localize, and interpret hydroacoustic noise in cavitating marine and hydraulic systems.
method: Adds vapor mass transfer, mixture compressibility, and pressure-rate effects to the acoustic equations.
Uses a source-resolved computational framework for cavitating multiphase hydroacoustics.
Applies the model to canonical 1D tests, a circular cylinder, and a NACA hydrofoil.
evidence_signal: Verification shows mesh and time-step refinement independence, PML boundary reflections are suppressed, and frequency-dependent attenuation matches Stokes' sound attenuation law.
watch_item: The framework still depends on accurate cavitation and source-term modeling, so predictive quality may be sensitive to closure assumptions and interface-capture resolution.
paper_title: Cavitation Acoustic Perturbation Equations: A Computational Framework for Source-Resolved Multiphase Hydroacoustics
